sections.title: Business goals and outcomes
sections.why: Anchors every later trade-off; a requirement that serves no goal is a candidate for Won't.
questions: What does success look like 12 months after go-live?
Which business KPI moves if this works, and by how much?
What happens if we do nothing?

sections.title: Users and personas
sections.why: Different users need different latency, UX and review steps.
questions: Who touches the output first, and who is accountable for it?
What does a great day look like for that person?

sections.title: Current process and pain points
sections.why: The as-is process is the baseline for value and the source of edge cases.
questions: Walk me through the last time you did this task, step by step.
Where do errors, rework or waiting happen today?

sections.title: Volumes and growth
sections.why: Drives model choice, batching, rate limits and cost.
questions: How many items per day/month, and what are the peaks?
What growth or new teams are expected in 12-24 months?

sections.title: Data sources and sensitivity
sections.why: Data availability and classification decide feasibility, residency and guardrails.
questions: Which systems hold the information a human uses today?
What is the classification of that data (PII, health, financial)?

sections.title: Integration points
sections.why: Read vs write access changes the risk profile (tools with side effects need approvals).
questions: Which systems must the solution read from and write to?
What APIs, auth mechanisms and rate limits exist?

sections.title: Constraints (latency, cost, compliance, timeline)
sections.why: Constraints are non-negotiable inputs; NFRs need measurable targets to be testable.
questions: What response time is acceptable, measured how (p95, time to first token)?
What budget or unit cost must we stay within?
Which regulations, residency or retention rules apply?

sections.title: Success metrics
sections.why: Without a baseline and target you cannot prove value or run evals.
questions: What is today's baseline for each KPI and how is it measured?
What target would make you call this a success?

sections.title: Failure handling and escalation
sections.why: LLMs are probabilistic; the design must say what happens when Claude is unsure or wrong.
questions: What should happen when the assistant is unsure, or a draft is wrong?
Who is the escalation point, and what is the fallback if the AI is unavailable?

sections.title: Risks and assumptions
sections.why: Unwritten assumptions become surprises; risks need owners and mitigations.
questions: What is the worst thing this system could do?
What are we assuming about data, contracts, people or timing?

human_review_policy.label: Human review before a letter is sent
human_review_policy.decision_owner: Head of Compliance (regulatory veto) with the VP Claims Operations
human_review_policy.compromise_hint: Claude drafts every letter; adjusters approve routine letters with one click while edit rates are measured. Revisit auto-send only with evidence (e.g. 3 months of <1% material edits) and written Compliance sign-off.

phase1_scope.label: Phase-1 scope: injury claims (medical data)
phase1_scope.compromise_hint: Phase 1 on property and auto claims; injury claims in phase 2 after a DPIA and a red-team of PHI handling. Use the overnight batch path for the injury backlog only once controls are proven.

go_live_date.label: Go-live date
go_live_date.decision_owner: Executive sponsor, informed by the Platform delivery plan
go_live_date.compromise_hint: Pilot with one adjuster team by January 15; general availability on March 1 after the security review.

ai_budget.label: AI usage budget
ai_budget.compromise_hint: Express the budget both ways: cost per letter and a monthly cap. Model the cost per letter in design (model choice, caching, batch for backlog) and agree which number wins.

latency_target.label: Latency target
latency_target.compromise_hint: Adopt the measurable target (time to first token <= 2 s, p95 full draft <= 10 s, streamed) and confirm with the sponsor that it satisfies 'fast'.

followup_templates.vague_nfr: You said "{quote}". What measurable target should we commit to for {category} - metric, threshold and how it is measured?
followup_templates.unmeasured_nfr: "{statement}" has no measurable target yet. How should we measure {category}, and what threshold is acceptable?
followup_templates.missing_owner: Who will own {req_id} "{statement}" after go-live (accountable for content, changes and approvals)?
followup_templates.conflict: {a_name} wants "{a_stance}"; {b_name} wants "{b_stance}". Decision owner: {owner}. Which option do we commit to for phase 1? Option to table: {hint}
followup_templates.no_baseline: What is today's baseline for "{metric}", and how is it measured?
followup_templates.unverified_quote: The extracted evidence for {ref} ("{quote}") is not verbatim in the transcript. Please confirm the stakeholder's exact words.
